content:
Dev Patel: Heads up — got a customer report of output drift and we can’t confidently answer “what changed” for *their* account. We can see global model promotions but not per-account routing/version history.

Dev Patel: Is there any internal view/export that shows, for account X:
- which model version/variant actually served requests (last 7–14 days)
- whether they were in a canary/A-B
- when routing policy changed (region fallback, capacity tier, etc)

SupportBot: Created Jira ticket SUP-28429 “Customer reports output regression after silent model change”.

Miguel Santos: +1, this comes up a lot with enterprise. Even when we tell them “we didn’t change your pinned model”, they ask for evidence.

Liam O'Rourke: This is Lattice (Dedicated) btw. They’re on `rw-chat` with a pinned major, but they think the quant profile changed. They’re asking for “exact version string and change log” for the last week.

Nora Ahmed: What do we have today? I’ve been grepping control plane logs and it’s messy. We need a Support-friendly artifact.

Chloe Martin: Today Console doesn’t expose per-account model change history. Internally we have:
- model registry promotions (global)
- rollout service logs for cohort assignments (not aggregated)
- request logs (if you have trace IDs)

Chloe Martin: We *don’t* have a single endpoint that says “account -> effective model version over time”. That’s exactly what the model metadata/changelog work is trying to fix.

Dev Patel: Understood, but we need an interim answer this week. Customer is asking for timeline + rollback guidance.

Jada Williams: For a stopgap, we can query the rollout assignment table + the “model version promoted” events, but it’s not self-serve. It’s also easy to mess up when there are fallback regions.

Jada Williams: If you can provide:
- org_id / account slug
- model handle
- approx timeframe
…I can run an internal query and send back a summary.

Ethan Park: Control plane emits events on promotions/metadata changes in staging, prod is partially rolled out. The missing piece is joining events to *policy resolution* (which version was selected for that account + deployment mode).

Ethan Park: We can also pull from request logs by org_id for Hosted, but Dedicated depends on the tenant logging config.

Miguel Santos: For enterprise we need something we can attach to the ticket: “Between Mar 31 10:00 UTC and Apr 2 18:00 UTC you were served vX.Y.Z (variant A) due to rollout cohort; no config changes on your side.”

Connor O'Brien: Release Eng POV: we’re adding release-note preview checks, but that still won’t answer per-account “effective version.” We need audit/query tooling.

Connor O'Brien: Do we have the internal admin surface from pr-18458 enabled yet? I remember an `/admin/audit/model-changes` endpoint mention.

Chloe Martin: The admin query endpoint exists behind RBAC, but it’s model-level and event-level. It doesn’t do account scoping. Also we need to be careful what we paste to customers (internal notes / redacted fields).

Nora Ahmed: What’s the minimum that would help Support?
- model identifier
- resolved model version (including quant profile)
- deployment (Hosted/Dedicated)
- region
- rollout phase/cohort
- timestamp range

Nora Ahmed: No internal-only notes, just “category + customer-safe summary” + link to public release notes if available.

Dev Patel: Yes. Also if we can say “no breaking changes” + “known issues” + “rollback option: pin version X”.

Liam O'Rourke: They specifically want to know if there was a tokenizer/runtime change.

Jada Williams: Tokenizer/runtime requirements are in the new metadata schema, but older records are inconsistent. I can include what we have (and flag gaps).

Ethan Park: I can help with a one-off export for this account:
1) Look up the tenant’s routing policy snapshot history
2) Pull rollout cohort assignment events
3) Join with model promotion events
4) Produce a short timeline

Ethan Park: But we should treat it as internal evidence; customer-facing needs to go through the redaction rules.

Miguel Santos: Can we standardize a “Support response template” for these cases? Even if it’s manual right now.

Chloe Martin: I can draft a template + checklist:
- confirm pinned version / policy
- check for rollout enrollment
- check for fallback routing
- check for recent metadata changes (quant profile, runtime)
- share customer-safe release note link if exists

Chloe Martin: Longer term this becomes Console “Model change history” + per-account visibility for Support roles.

Dev Patel: Action items?

Jada Williams: I’ll run the query for Lattice today if Liam drops org_id + model handle in the Jira.

Ethan Park: I’ll coordinate with Jada on the join logic and make sure we don’t misattribute fallback traffic.

Connor O'Brien: I’ll ping Security about what fields are safe to copy-paste externally (and whether we can generate a “public-only” export automatically).

Miguel Santos: I’ll add a note in SUP-28429 that this is a recurring requirement and link it to the model metadata/changelog epic.

Dev Patel: Thanks all. Liam, please put details in SUP-28429 + include a couple example request IDs if you have them. We need to reply to the customer by EOD tomorrow.
